calls: stats::t.test(y ~ group, var.equal = FALSE) + rstatix::cohens_d(var.equal = FALSE)
model: Welch two-sample t-test: two independent groups, unequal variances allowed
effect_size: Cohen's d (root-mean-square SD, matches Welch), Hedges' g
checks: extreme outliers per group; Shapiro-Wilk per group; Levene (median centre) and Fligner-Killeen
reference: Welch 1947 Biometrika 34:28; Cohen 1988 Statistical Power Analysis; Kassambara rstatix (CRAN)

calls: stats::t.test(y ~ group, var.equal = TRUE) + rstatix::cohens_d(var.equal = TRUE)
model: Student two-sample t-test: two independent groups, equal variances
checks: extreme outliers per group; Shapiro-Wilk per group; Levene (median centre) and Fligner-Killeen
reference: Student 1908 Biometrika 6:1; Cohen 1988; Kassambara rstatix (CRAN)

calls: stats::t.test(x, y, paired = TRUE) + rstatix::cohens_d(paired = TRUE)
model: paired t-test: two measurements on the same subjects
effect_size: Cohen's d of the differences (d_z), Hedges' g
checks: extreme outliers and Shapiro-Wilk of the differences
reference: Student 1908; Cohen 1988; Kassambara rstatix (CRAN)

calls: afex::aov_car(y ~ Error(subject/(within)), type = 3) + emmeans::emmeans(model = "multivariate")
model: repeated-measures ANOVA: every subject measured at every level of the within-subject factors
effect_size: generalized eta squared (ges), partial eta squared (pes)
posthoc: emmeans pairwise or vs-control contrasts; multivariate model for within-subject contrasts (no sphericity assumption)
checks: extreme outliers per cell (3 IQR); Shapiro-Wilk on residuals; Mauchly sphericity
reference: Singmann et al. afex (CRAN); Greenhouse & Geisser 1959 Psychometrika 24:95; Bakeman 2005 Behav Res Methods 37:379; Lenth emmeans (CRAN)
alternative: Friedman test (friedman) or the mixed model (lmer), which keeps subjects with missing cells

calls: afex::aov_car(y ~ between + Error(subject/(within)), type = 3) + emmeans::emmeans(model = "multivariate")
model: mixed (split-plot) ANOVA: between-subject factors, every subject measured at every level of the within-subject factors
correction: Greenhouse-Geisser for within-subject terms; Mauchly's test reported
effect_size: generalized eta squared (ges), partial eta squared (pes)
posthoc: emmeans pairwise or vs-control contrasts, simple effects for interactions
checks: extreme outliers per cell (3 IQR); Shapiro-Wilk on residuals; Levene per within-subject cell; Mauchly sphericity
reference: Singmann et al. afex (CRAN); Greenhouse & Geisser 1959; Bakeman 2005; Lenth emmeans (CRAN)
alternative: the mixed model (lmer), which keeps subjects with missing cells

calls: afex::aov_car(y ~ factors + Error(unit), type = 3) + emmeans::emmeans
model: factorial ANOVA, one observation per experimental unit; blocks (fixed or random intercept) as an additive term
test_statistic: F per term (type III, sum-to-zero contrasts)
effect_size: generalized eta squared (ges), partial eta squared (pes)
posthoc: emmeans pairwise or vs-control contrasts, simple effects for interactions
checks: extreme outliers per cell (3 IQR); Shapiro-Wilk on residuals; Levene across cells
reference: Singmann et al. afex (CRAN); Fox & Weisberg car::Anova; Olejnik & Algina 2003 Psychol Methods 8:434; Lenth emmeans (CRAN)

calls: stats::oneway.test(y ~ group, var.equal = FALSE) + rstatix::games_howell_test
model: Welch one-way ANOVA: several independent groups, unequal variances allowed
checks: extreme outliers per group; Shapiro-Wilk per group; Levene and Fligner-Killeen
reference: Welch 1951 Biometrika 38:330; Games & Howell 1976 J Educ Stat 1:113; Kassambara rstatix (CRAN)

calls: stats::wilcox.test(y ~ group) + rstatix::wilcox_effsize
model: Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann-Whitney U): two independent groups, ranks
reference: Wilcoxon 1945 Biometrics Bull 1:80; Mann & Whitney 1947 Ann Math Stat 18:50; Kassambara rstatix (CRAN)

calls: stats::wilcox.test(x, y, paired = TRUE) + rstatix::wilcox_effsize(paired = TRUE)
model: Wilcoxon signed-rank: two measurements on the same subjects; differences assumed symmetric
reference: Wilcoxon 1945; Kassambara rstatix (CRAN)
alternative: sign test (sign_test) for clearly asymmetric differences; paired t (t_test_paired)

calls: stats::binom.test(number of positive differences, non-zero differences, 0.5)
model: sign test: direction of paired differences only; ties dropped
reference: Dixon & Mood 1946 JASA 41:557; Conover 1999 Practical Nonparametric Statistics
alternative: Wilcoxon signed-rank (wilcoxon_signed_rank) when differences are symmetric

calls: stats::kruskal.test(y ~ group) + rstatix::kruskal_effsize + rstatix::dunn_test
model: Kruskal-Wallis: several independent groups, ranks
reference: Kruskal & Wallis 1952 JASA 47:583; Dunn 1964 Technometrics 6:241; Tomczak & Tomczak 2014 Trends Sport Sci 21:19

calls: stats::friedman.test(y ~ group | subject or block) + rstatix::friedman_effsize + stats::pairwise.wilcox.test(paired = TRUE)
model: Friedman: one factor, every subject (or block of an RCBD) at every level once, ranks within subject
reference: Friedman 1937 JASA 32:675; Kendall & Babington Smith 1939; Kassambara rstatix (CRAN)

calls: stats::prop.test(successes, n) (Yates correction for two groups)
model: test of equal proportions across independent groups (z-test for two groups, chi-squared for more)
test_statistic: X-squared (= z squared for two groups)
effect_size: difference in proportions with CI and Cohen's h (two groups)
checks: expected counts (Fisher's exact test when any is below stat_rules.json min_expected)
reference: Newcombe 1998 Stat Med 17:873; Cohen 1988

calls: stats::fisher.test(table(group, outcome)) + rstatix::pairwise_fisher_test
model: Fisher's exact test of independence between group and a binary outcome
reference: Fisher 1935 J R Stat Soc 98:39; Agresti 2002 Categorical Data Analysis

calls: stats::mcnemar.test(table(level1, level2)) (continuity correction); exact binomial on the discordant pairs when they are few (stat_rules.json mcnemar_exact_max)
model: McNemar test: a yes/no outcome measured twice on the same subjects (or matched pairs)
effect_size: conditional odds ratio of the discordant pairs with exact CI
reference: McNemar 1947 Psychometrika 12:153; Agresti 2002 Categorical Data Analysis

calls: rstatix::cochran_qtest(y ~ level | subject) + rstatix::pairwise_mcnemar_test
model: Cochran's Q: a yes/no outcome on the same subjects under 3+ conditions
reference: Cochran 1950 Biometrika 37:256; Kassambara rstatix (CRAN)
alternative: McNemar for two levels; GLMM (glmer binomial) for the model

calls: stats::mantelhaen.test(table(group, outcome, block))
model: Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test: a yes/no outcome by group within blocks (strata), pooled
effect_size: common odds ratio with CI (two groups)
reference: Mantel & Haenszel 1959 J Natl Cancer Inst 22:719; Agresti 2002

calls: stats::prop.trend.test(successes, n, score = dose values)
model: Cochran-Armitage test for a linear trend in proportions over an ordered or numeric factor
reference: Cochran 1954 Biometrics 10:417; Armitage 1955 Biometrics 11:375
alternative: logistic regression on the dose (the engine)

calls: stats::chisq.test(table(group, category)) + rstatix::cramer_v; Fisher when an expected count < stat_rules.json min_expected
model: chi-squared test of independence between group and an unordered category
reference: Pearson 1900; Cramer 1946; Agresti 2002

calls: survival::survfit + survival::survdiff (+ strata(block)) + Cox fit from the engine (cox.zph)
model: Kaplan-Meier per group (medians, quantiles, landmarks), log-rank (stratified by the design blocks), hazard ratios and the PH check from the Cox engine, RMST (two groups)
effect_size: hazard ratio (Cox), RMST difference and ratio
checks: cox.zph; events per Cox coefficient; median not reached
reference: Kaplan & Meier 1958; Mantel 1966; Cox 1972; Grambsch & Therneau 1994; Royston & Parmar 2013

calls: survival::survdiff(rho = 1) or base R (Fleming-Harrington, Gehan, Tarone-Ware; = survdiff / survMisc)
model: Gehan, Tarone-Ware, Peto-Peto or Fleming-Harrington weighted log-rank, one prespecified weight
reference: Fleming & Harrington 1991; Peto & Peto 1972

calls: survival::survreg(dist = weibull, exponential, lognormal, loglogistic); lowest AIC
model: accelerated failure time model
effect_size: time ratio; Weibull hazard ratio = TR^(-shape)
reference: Wei 1992 Stat Med 11:1871

calls: cmprsk::cuminc + cmprsk::crr; cause-specific Cox from the engine
model: cumulative incidence per cause, Gray test, Fine-Gray model (event codes 2+)
reference: Gray 1988; Fine & Gray 1999

calls: KMsurv::lifetab per group
model: actuarial life table on intervals
reference: Cutler & Ederer 1958 J Chronic Dis 8:699
